info.name: autorouter.aero — NOTAM (StackChan flight-radar)
info.description:
Exercises exactly the two calls `firmware/flight-radar/main.cpp` makes for its NOTAM view: the OAuth 2.0 token, then the NOTAM query. Written from the CODE, not from the vendor docs, so what you test here is what the robot does.

## Credentials never live in this file

`user` and `pass` are declared empty and typed `secret`. Fill them in Postman (collection variables, or better an environment) — this file is committed, and the account is your autorouter LOGIN, not a throwaway API key: it can file flight plans. Same rule as `sdcard/stackchan-companion/config.yaml`.

## Tokens are the scarce resource, not the requests

A token lives SEVEN DAYS and an account may hold only TWENTY active ones. Minting one per test run is a countdown to a 403 `toomanytokens` that then lasts a week. So the NOTAM requests REUSE `{{token}}` and mint only when it is empty — the same optimistic policy as the firmware and `tools/probes/autorouter-notam.py`. Run `01 Token` once; run it again only when a request comes back 401/403.

## The 403 that is not what it looks like

autorouter answers 403 for two unrelated things and the remedies are OPPOSITE:

- `"error": "privileges"` — the account is fine but API access is a SEPARATE permission, granted on request through a support ticket.
- `"error": "toomanytokens"` — nothing to ask anyone. The account is healthy and merely holds 20 live tokens. Wait for the oldest to expire, or revoke them.

The tests below read that field and say which one it is. Getting this wrong cost a week of waiting on a support ticket for a perfectly good account (2026-08-01).

Filled by '01 Token'. Reused by every NOTAM request; 20 active per account, 7 days each.
Aerodrome. FMEE = Roland Garros, La Réunion — the radar's default station.
Flight Information Region. Optional: the aerodrome list misses en-route NOTAMs (airspace, navaids) that only the FIR publishes.
The firmware asks for 100 and keeps at most NOTAM_MAX = 40 after filtering.
